correctness.rationale: PASS: A commuting involutive family is a labelled F_2^k-set, whose transitive orbits are G/H with independent component multiplicities. Atomic two-variable pair-type counts and their vertex-signature partitions are determined by N_tau, and equal N_tau give a stable counting-bisimulation; conversely each N_tau is definable with C^2 counting. The minimum orbit size realizing a signature with r nonidentity blocks is 2^ceil(log2(r+1)); repetitions fill all multiples, giving the Stirling product. Distinct subgroup signatures cannot arise for quotient dimension <=2, proving the 7-vertex cutoff. Independent enumeration of the 16 subgroups of F_2^3 and orbit-multiset partition series reproduced I_3(8)=611, C_3(8)=610, precisely one class of two isotypes.
